
# Daily–monthly consistency

This descriptive comparison links each monthly submission to that participant's daily submissions in the same calendar month.

**What it shows.** Monthly symptom reporting is compared between participant-months with at least one corresponding positive daily report and those with no positive daily report.

**Why it matters.** Strong agreement supports the idea that daily and monthly instruments are capturing related experiences. Disagreement is not automatically an error: monthly recall, missed daily forms, question wording, and different reference periods can all produce genuine differences.

```{r}
#| label: daily-monthly-consistency
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10

daily_by_month <- daily_data |>
  mutate(reference_month = format(report_date, "%Y-%m")) |>
  group_by(participant_id, reference_month) |>
  summarise(
    daily_submissions = n(),
    daily_any_bleeding = as.integer(any(menstrual_bleeding_yesterday == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    daily_any_pain = as.integer(any(menstrual_pain_yesterday == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

linked_months <- monthly_data |>
  inner_join(daily_by_month, by = c("participant_id", "reference_month"))

summarise_consistency <- function(data, daily_variable, monthly_variable, symptom_label) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c(0L, 1L), function(daily_value) {
    relevant_data <- data |>
      filter(.data[[daily_variable]] == daily_value)
    clustered_factor_summary(
      relevant_data,
      response_factor = factor(
        relevant_data[[monthly_variable]],
        levels = c(0, 1),
        labels = c("No", "Yes")
      ),
      question = symptom_label,
      count_name = "positive_records"
    ) |>
      filter(response == "Yes") |>
      transmute(
        records = denominator,
        percent,
        ci_low,
        ci_high,
        symptom = symptom_label,
        daily_report = if_else(
          daily_value == 1,
          "At least one positive daily report",
          "No positive daily report"
        )
      )
  }))
}

consistency_plot <- bind_rows(
  summarise_consistency(
    linked_months,
    "daily_any_bleeding",
    "menstrual_bleeding_last_month",
    "Monthly bleeding report"
  ),
  summarise_consistency(
    linked_months,
    "daily_any_pain",
    "menstrual_pain_last_month",
    "Monthly pain report"
  )
)

ggplot(consistency_plot, aes(percent, daily_report)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#167c77", width = .62) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high),
    orientation = "y",
    height = .18,
    linewidth = .5
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%s  %s", records, percent(percent, accuracy = .1))),
            hjust = -.05, size = 3.5) +
  facet_grid(symptom ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1.12), breaks = seq(0, 1, .25),
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Percent reporting the symptom in the monthly form",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Whiskers are participant-clustered 95% confidence intervals."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
        plot.margin = margin(8, 48, 8, 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: agreement-table

agreement <- tibble(
  Symptom = c("Bleeding", "Pain"),
  `Linked participant-months` = nrow(linked_months),
  `Daily/monthly agreement` = c(
    mean(linked_months$daily_any_bleeding == linked_months$menstrual_bleeding_last_month),
    mean(linked_months$daily_any_pain == linked_months$menstrual_pain_last_month)
  )
) |>
  mutate(`Daily/monthly agreement` = percent(`Daily/monthly agreement`, accuracy = .1))

kable(agreement, align = c("l", "r", "r"))
```

## Data-quality checks

These checks identify structural problems that could invalidate interpretation—for example, duplicate records, skip-logic violations, unmatched SVG codes, or impossible cycle lengths. A zero means the specific issue was not found. Long inferred cycles are shown as review flags rather than errors because they may be genuine or may reflect an unobserved intervening onset.

```{r}
#| label: data-quality

data_quality <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Daily: duplicate participant-date records",
    "Daily: report dated before programme start",
    "Daily: bleeding follow-up outside bleeding skip condition",
    "Daily: pain follow-up outside pain skip condition",
    "Monthly: duplicate participant-month records",
    "Monthly: bleeding follow-up outside bleeding skip condition",
    "Monthly: clot comparison outside clot skip condition",
    "Monthly: pain comparison outside pain skip condition",
    "Monthly: discharge comparison outside discharge skip condition",
    "Monthly: more than two bleeding products/materials",
    "Monthly: 'no product' selected with another option",
    "Unmatched symmetric body-map response codes",
    "Unmatched detailed body-map response codes",
    "Inferred completed cycle length is zero or negative",
    "Inferred completed cycle shorter than configured onset interval",
    "Completed inferred cycles above review threshold (not excluded)",
    "Daily record assigned to more than one inferred cycle"
  ),
  Issues = c(
    sum(duplicated(daily_data[c("participant_id", "report_date")])),
    sum(daily_data$report_date < daily_data$programme_start_date, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(
      daily_data$menstrual_bleeding_yesterday == 0 &
        (!is.na(daily_data$bleeding_amount_yesterday) |
         !is.na(daily_data$bleeding_amount_expected_yesterday)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    sum(
      daily_data$menstrual_pain_yesterday == 0 &
        (!is.na(daily_data$pain_amount_yesterday) |
         !is.na(daily_data$pain_duration_yesterday) |
         (!is.na(daily_data[[location_field]]) & str_trim(daily_data[[location_field]]) != "")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    sum(duplicated(monthly_data[c("participant_id", "reference_month")])),
    sum(
      monthly_data$menstrual_bleeding_last_month == 0 &
        (!is.na(monthly_data$clots_last_month) |
         (!is.na(monthly_data$bleeding_product_material) & monthly_data$bleeding_product_material != "") |
         !is.na(monthly_data$bleeding_days_change)), na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    sum(monthly_data$clots_last_month != 1 &
          (!is.na(monthly_data$clot_number_change) | !is.na(monthly_data$clot_size_change)),
        na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(monthly_data$menstrual_pain_last_month == 0 &
          (!is.na(monthly_data$pain_severity_change) | !is.na(monthly_data$pain_days_change) |
           !is.na(monthly_data$pain_location_change)), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(monthly_data$vaginal_discharge_last_month == 0 & !is.na(monthly_data$discharge_change),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    sum(str_count(coalesce(monthly_data$bleeding_product_material, ""), "\\S+") > 2),
    sum(str_detect(coalesce(monthly_data$bleeding_product_material, ""), "(^| )10( |$)") &
          str_count(coalesce(monthly_data$bleeding_product_material, ""), "\\S+") > 1),
    length(bodymap$unknown),
    length(detailed_bodymap$unknown),
    sum(completed_cycles$cycle_length <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(completed_cycles$cycle_length < minimum_cycle_gap_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(completed_cycles$cycle_length > long_cycle_review_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(duplicated(cycle_daily[c("participant_id", "report_date")]))
  )
)

kable(data_quality, align = c("l", "r"))
```

## Analysis notes

- Daily rows are repeated submissions. Daily symptom percentages use daily submissions as their denominator.
- Both body maps use pain-positive daily submissions and all unique participants as the denominator. Each person contributes at most once per detailed or symmetric region across the observation period.
- Programme cycles are numbered separately for each participant from the first qualifying CD1 after programme start. Completed cycle lengths remain in days and are not normalised to 28 days.
- Cycle-specific prevalence counts each participant once per region and programme cycle. The timing heatmap counts each participant once per region, programme cycle, and cycle day; its cell denominator is participants with a report for that cycle and day.
- Monthly rows are participant-months. Monthly conditional questions use only rows for which the XLSForm makes the question relevant.
- Daily–monthly comparisons require a stable participant ID and a correctly aligned calendar month.
- This is descriptive analysis. It does not test causal relationships or make clinical interpretations.
- The dummy-data pain distribution is intentionally pelvic, abdominal, lumbosacral, breast, and head weighted for testing; it is illustrative and is not a clinical prevalence estimate.

## Technical appendix: detailed ever-reported pain location map

This version retains every original SVG region, including left/right and dorsal/ventral distinctions. Locations come only from pain-positive daily submissions; percentages use all unique participants as the denominator, and each participant contributes at most once per detailed region across the observation period.

**What it answers.** “Did this participant ever report pain in this exact anatomical region during follow-up?” Repeated reports in the same region do not increase that participant's contribution.

**Why it is in the appendix.** The detailed map preserves laterality and body surface for clinical or instrument-development review, while the symmetric map earlier in the report provides the clearer primary summary.

```{r}
#| label: detailed-body-map
#| results: asis

detailed_map_html <- tags$div(
  id = "bodymap-report-detailed",
  class = "bodymap-report",
  tags$div(
    class = "bodymap-frame",
    HTML(detailed_bodymap$markup),
    tags$div(
      class = "tooltip bodymap-hover",
      role = "status",
      `aria-live` = "polite",
      tags$div(class = "tooltip-inner")
    )
  ),
  tags$div(
    class = "bodymap-legend",
    `aria-label` = "Colour scale: percent of all participants",
    tags$div(class = "bodymap-gradient"),
    tags$div(
      class = "bodymap-legend-labels",
      tags$span("0%"),
      tags$span("Percent of all participants"),
      tags$span(sprintf("%.1f%%", detailed_bodymap$maximum))
    )
  ),
  tags$div(
    class = "bodymap-note",
    "Hover over or focus a detailed body region to see its participant count and percentage."
  )
)

cat("```{=html}\n", as.character(detailed_map_html), "\n```\n", sep = "")

if (length(detailed_bodymap$unknown) > 0) {
  warning_html <- tags$div(
    class = "bodymap-warning",
    tags$strong("Unmatched detailed response codes: "),
    paste(detailed_bodymap$unknown, collapse = ", ")
  )
  cat("```{=html}\n", as.character(warning_html), "\n```\n", sep = "")
}
```
